title: The dog and the gull
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The dog meets the gull. The real one, on the seawall. Two strokes of a bird and four of a dog. The strip has drawn its own margin and it's barking at it.

panels.composition: The seawall at the end of main street. A gull on it. BARNABY on the walk below, rigid. WOOD with the leash.

image.prompt: a gull perched on a low concrete seawall with a small dog on the walkway below staring up at it, a young man holding the leash, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The gull. Two strokes. Exactly the margin's.

image.prompt: close on a gull on a seawall drawn in two simple strokes, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog barking. Four strokes. The gull not moving.

image.prompt: a small dog barking up at an unbothered gull on a seawall, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The gull lifting off, unhurried. The dog watching it go over the bay. Wood, to the leash.

balloons.text: You'll never get one. I never have.

image.prompt: a gull lifting lazily off a seawall over a gray bay while a small dog watches and a young man holds the leash, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The dog barks at the margin. 'I never have.'
